files.sourceInUseTitle: File is still used by a task
files.removeSourceConfirm: Remove this file from the files to send? Your original file will be kept.
files.receivingRestoreError: Reception could not be restored. Check the diagnostic log and try again.

service.entryHint: File transfers run as a separate ordinary-user service. Open its private management page; the daemon console login does not grant file access.
service.unavailable: The file service is unavailable. Check its status from the server terminal.
service.waiting: Receiving is enabled; waiting for the connection and file service to be ready.
service.offline: The mesh or file interface is not ready. Waiting for reconnection; you can still turn reception off or change automatic saving.
service.autoSaveHint: Save completed files to this directory without overwriting existing files. Received originals are retained until their records are removed.
service.issue: The file service needs attention. Check the server logs.
service.keyHint: Run calabi mesh files service web-url on the server as root or the file-service user to obtain your private access link.

web.title: Linux file transfers
web.loginHint: Open the private link printed by the Linux file agent, or enter its access key.
web.loginError: Unable to connect. Check the access key and file agent.
web.directoryError: Unable to read the Linux working directory.
web.directoryHint: Files are read from the configured Linux directory without making a copy.
web.saveHint: Save to the configured Linux directory. Existing files will not be overwritten.

errors.sourceInUse: This file is still used by a sending task. Remove its associated sent record in File transfers first. Pause or cancel the task first if it is still running.
errors.authorization: File transfer is not currently authorized. Check that both devices are connected and reception is enabled.
errors.identity: The file transfer identity changed or its certificate is unavailable. Check the certificate in settings.
errors.source: The original file was moved, deleted or changed. Choose it again.
errors.integrity: File verification failed. Please send the file again.
errors.storage: Not enough storage space. Free up space and retry.
errors.storageWrite: Could not save the file or task record. Check the storage location and retry.
errors.agent: The file transfer service is not ready. Reopen the app and retry.
errors.connection: Could not reach the other device. Check that it is online and accepting files, then retry.
errors.limit: The file or task limit has been reached. Clear old records and retry.
errors.restarted: The app restarted. Resume the transfer to continue.
errors.stale: This record is no longer available. Refresh the list and retry.
errors.interrupted: The transfer was interrupted. You can retry.
errors.generic: The operation could not be completed. Retry, or check file-transfer entries on the Logs page.

files.updateSender: Update the sending client to pause reception
files.recordsFoot: Incoming files need confirmation · Completed files can be saved elsewhere
files.waitingBatch: Waiting for the remaining files in this batch…
files.confirmHint: The recipient needs to confirm before receiving.
files.identityUnavailable: File identity information is currently unavailable.
files.bridgeUnavailable: The desktop file interface is not ready. Quit the old desktop app and open the updated preview app.
files.noDevices: No devices in the current mesh
files.devicesError: Could not load devices. Please retry.

targetStatus.notReady: File transfers are not ready on this device
targetStatus.receivingOff: Reception is off on this device

files.preparePeer: Make sure the device is online and open File transfers in an updated client or run its file agent. This page updates automatically when ready.
files.enablePeerReception: Enable Allow incoming file requests on the receiving device to send files.
files.identityDue: The certificate expires within 30 days. Renew it when transfers are idle.
files.identityConfirm: This stops reception and cancels unfinished file transfers for every account and organization used by this OS user. Completed files, staged sources and history are retained. The mesh device identity is unchanged. Turn reception on again when ready.
files.title: File transfers
files.hint: Send files to online devices in your network. Incoming files need your confirmation and use the existing direct or relay connection.
files.unavailable: File transfers are available in the Windows and macOS desktop preview.
files.name: Name
files.removeConfirm: Remove this local record or cached file? Files saved elsewhere are retained.
files.peerUnavailable: This device is offline or has not enabled file transfers.

states.cancelPending: Cancelled; waiting to notify the peer (record can be removed)

topbar.keyOwnerUnknown: Running on an API key (issuer not recorded)
topbar.ownEdgeOfflineTip: Your self-hosted node is offline; endpoint traffic is temporarily routed through the platform. It will switch back automatically once your node is up.

orgSwitch.body1: After switching, this client re-handshakes with the edge node and takes over the endpoints of "{{name}}".
orgSwitch.body2: The endpoints of the current organization "{{name}}" will go offline temporarily (they recover automatically when you switch back).

region.reconnectBody: Retry connecting to the edge nodes in this region.
region.switchBody1: After switching, this client reconnects to the edge nodes in region "{{region}}".
region.switchBody2: Endpoints in the original region (their external addresses are pinned to that region) will no longer be reachable through this client; you'll need to recreate them in the new region (the external address will change). Node switching within the same region is automatic and unaffected.
region.parkedNote: The edge nodes in the current region are unreachable. The client keeps retrying in the background; switching region from the top-right reconnects immediately.

affinity.toOwnBody: This client will reconnect to your self-hosted node; endpoint data egresses from your own server (bandwidth/traffic is yours). The mesh home relay follows, preferring your own relays.
affinity.toPlatformBody: This client will reconnect to a platform edge node; endpoint data egresses from the platform (rate-limited/metered per your plan). The mesh home relay follows, moving to a platform relay.
affinity.bodyNote: Switching reconnects the edge node; the endpoint's external address (pinned to a specific node) will change, so existing endpoints must be recreated.

overview.readOnlyDesc: Overdue billing or an exceeded quota puts the account in read-only mode, where new endpoints can't be created. Open the console for details.
overview.quotaExceededDesc: Once exceeded, all existing endpoints keep working but no new ones can be added. Upgrade your plan or wait for next month's reset.
overview.quotaExceededDescNoUpgrade: Once exceeded, all existing endpoints keep working but no new ones can be added. Resets at the start of next month.
overview.selfHostedNotBilled: Self-hosted node · not counted toward plan
overview.edgeSelfTip: This endpoint currently routes through your org's self-hosted edge node (where switching the data node to "self-hosted" moves it).
overview.relaySelfTip: Currently homed on your org's self-hosted relay (where switching the data node to "self-hosted" moves it).
overview.notifReconnectingBody: The session with the edge node dropped; reconnecting automatically.
overview.notifFatalBody: Check the Logs page to find the cause.
overview.notifQuota100Body: Upgrade your plan, or wait for the next calendar month to reset.
overview.notifQuota100BodyNoUpgrade: Wait for the next calendar month to reset, or ask your platform administrator.
overview.meshDatapathPendingTip: The relay is known; the mesh datapath is still coming up.

tunnels.awaitingApprovalTip: This organization reviews the endpoints its members create. An admin has to approve this one in the console before it serves anything.
tunnels.rejectedTip: An admin turned this endpoint down.
tunnels.offlineNotConnectedTip: This client isn't connected to an edge node; the endpoint is temporarily offline.
tunnels.edgeDownTip: The edge node #{{id}} hosting this endpoint is offline; the endpoint is temporarily unavailable.
tunnels.onlineTip: Online — endpoint is live and serving.
tunnels.probeOkTip: Local probe OK ({{ms}}ms, {{n}} in a row)
tunnels.probeFailTip: Local probe failed: {{err}} ({{n}} in a row)
tunnels.serverOnlineTip: Online — served by another session of this client (e.g. a foreground 'calabi http'), or syncing
tunnels.heldByOtherClientTip: This endpoint is bound to another client in your org and isn't running on this machine.
tunnels.onlineOtherClientTip: Online — served by another client in your org, not this machine.

takeover.tip: Bring this endpoint to this machine
takeover.warnLocal: This machine will forward to the local address below — make sure that service is actually running here.
takeover.warnOther: The other client will stop serving this endpoint.
takeover.warnGap: The external address stays the same, but expect a brief interruption while it moves here.
takeover.localTip: The local service on THIS machine to forward to (often differs from the original machine).
takeover.crossEdgeTip: This endpoint runs in another region/edge. Its external address is bound to that edge — an http/https subdomain is pinned there and a tcp/udp port is allocated there — so taking it over to this client would change (or break) the external address. Switch this client to the endpoint's region first, or recreate the endpoint here.

ipPolicy.title: IP access control
ipPolicy.hint: Allow or deny callers by source IP / CIDR (one per line). Enforced at the edge.
ipPolicy.allow: Allowlist — only these may connect (leave empty to allow all)
ipPolicy.deny: Denylist — always blocked (wins over the allowlist)
ipPolicy.applyNote: Applied at the edge on save — no reconnect needed.
ipPolicy.sourceFollowHint: Follows the organization policy “{{name}}”. Edits to the policy reach this endpoint automatically.

basicAuth.title: Basic authentication
basicAuth.hint: Require a username + password before a request reaches your service (HTTP/HTTPS endpoints). Passwords are hashed.

rateLimit.title: Rate limit
rateLimit.hint: Cap the rate of new connections to this endpoint (protects your upstream from floods). 0 / empty = unlimited.
rateLimit.perIPSuggest: Only the endpoint-wide cap is set: one caller can drain it and everyone else is turned away. Consider setting a per-IP cap as well.

headers.title: Request headers
headers.hint: Rewrite headers sent to your upstream (HTTP/HTTPS). Framing headers (Content-Length, etc.) can't be changed.
headers.name: Header

oauth.title: OAuth authentication
oauth.hint: Require a sign-in with an identity provider before anyone reaches your service (HTTP/HTTPS).
oauth.callbackHint: Register this redirect/callback URL in your OAuth app:
oauth.allowEmails: Allowed emails (one per line; empty = any signed-in user)
oauth.ownConfig: Configure this endpoint on its own
oauth.fromPolicyHint: Uses the organization login policy “{{name}}”. Provider, client ID and who may sign in come from that policy — change them under Policy.

security.title: Access control
security.lockedNotice: Some features require a plan upgrade to use: {{features}}.
security.lockedNoticeContact: Your plan doesn't include: {{features}}. Ask your platform administrator to enable them.
security.barePortNote: {{type}} endpoints forward bytes as-is and never read the request, so they only take IP access control and rate limits. Basic authentication, OAuth authentication and request headers work on HTTP/HTTPS endpoints only.
security.inertStored: This endpoint has the settings below saved, but they have no effect on a {{type}} endpoint. Saving keeps them as they are:
security.stillActive: Your plan doesn't include the settings below, but they are already set on this endpoint and still in effect. Saving keeps them as they are; click Remove to drop one.

err.headerForbidden: The header “{{value}}” can't be rewritten (it affects the transport framing).
err.oauthCredentials: The OAuth login needs a Client ID and a Client Secret.

edit.title: Edit endpoint
edit.endpointFixed: Type and external address can't be changed — create a new endpoint to use a different one.
edit.offMachineTitle: This endpoint runs on another machine
edit.offMachineDesc: Editing the name and security policy applies remotely. But “local address” points at the upstream on the machine that actually serves this endpoint — not this one. To run it here instead, use Takeover.
edit.offMachineLocalHint: This address applies to the other machine serving this endpoint.

tunnels.deleteConfirmDesc: It's removed from the edge node immediately; if a client is running, related connections are cut.
tunnels.cappedTooltip: Plan limit reached {{count}}/{{max}}; upgrade or delete existing endpoints and try again.
tunnels.cappedTooltipNoUpgrade: Plan limit reached {{count}}/{{max}}; delete existing endpoints and try again.
tunnels.cappedAlertDesc: Upgrade your plan or delete existing endpoints for the "New endpoint" button to become available again.
tunnels.cappedAlertDescNoUpgrade: Delete existing endpoints for the "New endpoint" button to become available again.
tunnels.edgeSwitchMsg: Switched cross-region to new edge node #{{current}} (the region of node #{{previous}} is unavailable)
tunnels.edgeSwitchDesc1: This client is now connected to an edge node in
tunnels.edgeSwitchDesc2: . Endpoint domains created in the previous region are temporarily unreachable — the region-wide wildcard is pinned to the original region and cross-region nodes don't forward to each other. Wait for the original region to recover and reconnect, or
tunnels.edgeSwitchDeleteRebuild: delete the endpoint and recreate it in the current region
tunnels.edgeSwitchDesc3: (the external address will change). Node switching within the same region is transparent and doesn't affect endpoint access.
tunnels.emptyText: No endpoints yet · click "New endpoint" in the top-right
tunnels.regionFilteredDesc: These endpoints are pinned to edges in other regions and can't be served from here. Switch region above, or see every region at once in the web console.
tunnels.mismatchTip: The client is connected to edge #{{clientEdge}}, but this endpoint's domain is pinned to edge #{{boundEdge}}, so the external address is unreachable. Switch the client back to edge #{{boundEdge}}, or delete and recreate the endpoint on the current edge (the domain will change).
tunnels.pendingTip: Recorded on the server, but no node has taken it over yet. Usually the client simply hasn't connected; if it has, the node refused the claim and the client log says why.
tunnels.unverifiedTip: The node is serving this endpoint, but no client has reported a check of the local upstream, so whether it is reachable is unknown — this is not a fault. Endpoints created straight from the command line are never checked, nor are clients older than 1.10.0.
tunnels.upstreamDownTip: The client can't reach this endpoint's local upstream service.
tunnels.errorPortInUseTip: Remote port {{port}} is already taken on this node. Choose a different port, or remove the endpoint that holds it.
tunnels.memberCappedTooltip: You have used your endpoint allowance ({{count}}/{{max}}). Delete one, or ask an organization administrator to raise it.
tunnels.memberCappedTitle: You have used your endpoint allowance
tunnels.memberCappedDesc: An administrator set your limit at {{max}}; you are using {{count}}. Delete one, or ask them to raise it — this allowance is yours personally, so upgrading the plan will not move it.

wizard.publishBannerDesc: The local address is filled from the service; pick the endpoint's type and address below. This is a separate endpoint — it doesn't change the service's mesh access.
wizard.localAddrTip: The client forwards to this address, e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080
wizard.localAddrPublic: Use a local or LAN address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080 or a 10./192.168. host) — forwarding to an address on the internet is not allowed.
wizard.localAddrFormat: Enter host:port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080 or localhost:3000) or a bare port.
wizard.remotePortTip: Leave blank to let the server assign one
wizard.customDomainRequired: Self-hosted egress requires your own domain
wizard.customDomainTip: Current egress is your self-hosted node: the external address uses your own domain. Point it to your self-hosted node's external IP, then complete verification / certificate binding in the web console under "Domains".
wizard.subdomainTip: Prefix only (e.g. myapp); the full address = prefix + the platform region subdomain (auto-generated, not editable). Leave blank for a random one. Custom domains are only available on self-hosted egress.
wizard.subdomainPattern: Lowercase letters / digits / hyphens only, and may not start or end with a hyphen
wizard.subdomainFreePlaceholder: Free plan assigns a random subdomain (choose your own after upgrading)
wizard.subdomainFreePlaceholderNoUpgrade: A random subdomain is assigned automatically
wizard.countHint: This organization already has {{team}} endpoints; a new one is appended to the list
wizard.countHintShared: This organization already has {{team}} endpoints ({{mine}} on this client); a new one is appended to the list
wizard.domainNoCertHint: This domain has no certificate yet: HTTP works now; HTTPS starts working once you issue a certificate under “Domains” in the web console.
wizard.localServiceTip: How the client dials your local service: HTTP connects in the clear, HTTPS wraps the connection in TLS (self-signed certificates are accepted). TLS hands the connection to your service as is; your service completes the handshake with its own certificate.
wizard.checkFailHint: You can still create the endpoint — start the service and it will connect.
wizard.prefixCertNote: The HTTPS certificate is issued right after the endpoint is created — it takes a minute or two. HTTP works immediately.

reason.refused: Nothing is listening on that address yet.
reason.timeout: The address accepted nothing in time — it may be blocked by a firewall.
reason.unreachable: That address can't be reached from this machine.
reason.dns: That hostname doesn't resolve on this machine.
reason.tls: TLS failed. If your local service speaks plain HTTP, pick HTTP instead of HTTPS.
reason.http_5xx: The service answered, but with a server error.
reason.invalid: That address isn't a local one — an endpoint can only point at this machine or your own network.

wizard.preflightBody: You can create the endpoint anyway — it will connect as soon as the service is up.
wizard.prefixTipNode: Type a prefix only — the full address is <prefix>.{{suffix}}. Point *.{{suffix}} at {{ip}}, the node this client is connected to.
wizard.parentEmptyHint: This node serves no verified domain yet. Set its base_domain in the web console, and verify that domain under “Domains”.
wizard.apexInUse: {{name}} itself is already taken by the endpoint “{{tunnel}}”. Type a prefix.
wizard.ipSectionHint: Only the listed addresses may connect. The only option a raw-port endpoint has.
wizard.protNoneBlocked: Not now (not allowed in this organization)
wizard.protOpenList: This list contains 0.0.0.0/0 (or ::/0), which admits everyone and does not satisfy the organization’s access-protection requirement.
wizard.protPickPolicyFirst: Pick an IP policy, or switch back to “not now”.
wizard.protAddrsEmpty: Enter at least one address, or switch back to “not now” — an empty list is not a stricter rule, it is no rule, and the edge lets everyone in.
wizard.protNeeded: This organization requires an access policy for this kind of endpoint. Pick a policy or enter the addresses allowed to reach it.
wizard.protBarePortHelp: This organization requires TCP/UDP/TLS endpoints to carry an IP rule. A raw port has no login to attach, so an address list is the only thing that can turn anyone away.
wizard.protRequiredHelp: This organization requires every endpoint to have access protection.
wizard.protOptionalHelp: Optional — you can also add this from the endpoint's security settings later.
wizard.protNoDefaultWarn: This organization requires access protection but has no default IP policy, which means a command-line create (calabi http 8080) is refused outright. An administrator sets the default under Endpoints → Settings in the web console.
wizard.protNoDefaultWarnBarePort: This organization requires an IP rule on raw ports but has no default IP policy, so a command-line create (calabi tcp 5432) is refused unless it carries --ip-allow. An administrator sets the default under Endpoints → Settings in the web console.
wizard.basicAuthHint: A username and password are required to open the address. The password is sent in plain text, hashed by the server, and never sent back. Can be used together with an address list.
wizard.basicAuthIncomplete: One row has only a username or only a password. Finish it, or remove the row.
wizard.basicAuthNotForRawPort: Basic auth only works on HTTP/HTTPS endpoints — a raw port is byte passthrough, with no request to challenge.
wizard.doneSub: The external address is assigned and reachable now.
wizard.donePendingSub: An edge is claiming this endpoint and assigning its external address. This usually takes a few seconds.
wizard.donePendingNote: This page refreshes itself. You can also go back to the list, which follows the same change.
wizard.doneStalledTitle: No edge has taken this endpoint yet
wizard.doneStalledBody: This endpoint is bound to this machine, so the usual reason is that the daemon is not connected to an edge right now. The endpoint already exists — it gets claimed and given an external address automatically once the connection is back, so there is nothing to re-create.
wizard.doneMissingTitle: This endpoint is no longer in your list
wizard.doneMissingBody: The server no longer has this record (#{{id}}). It was either deleted, or replaced by a new row when a client claimed it. Check the endpoint list; if it really is gone, create it again and pass this number on to whoever runs the platform.
wizard.ipNeedPlan: This plan does not include IP access control. This organization does not require access protection, so the endpoint can be created as it is — upgrade if you want to restrict the source addresses.
wizard.ipNeedPlanNoUpgrade: This plan does not include IP access control. The organization does not require access protection, so the endpoint can be created as it is.
wizard.tlsNeedsDomain: TLS (needs a verified domain on your node)
wizard.tlsNeedsHttpsPort: TLS (the node has no HTTPS port)
wizard.tlsPrefixRequired: A TLS endpoint needs a name: your certificate has to match it
wizard.typeHelpHttps: The edge decrypts with a platform-issued certificate, then forwards to your service, so you can add OAuth sign-in, Basic auth and header rewrites. To keep your own certificate and have the edge not decrypt, choose TLS.
wizard.typeHelpTls: Your service uses its own certificate. The edge routes by domain name only and never decrypts, so it cannot see the content. Access control is IP rules and rate limits only.

inspector.title: Request inspector · {{name}}
inspector.noHttpHint: Only http / https endpoints are captured, and at least one visit is required.
inspector.replayTip: Resend this request to the local upstream

authGate.hint: If it stays unresponsive, check whether the daemon is running (tray → restart daemon)
authGate.serverUnreachableHint: The local daemon is running, but it can't reach the Calabi server (control plane). Check that the server is up and your network is connected.
authGate.daemonStarting: The local daemon is starting up...
authGate.daemonStartingHint: It's still initializing its connection — this usually clears within a few seconds.

settings.serviceHint: Register the daemon as a system service to auto-start on boot:
settings.serviceNote: Note: install / uninstall requires administrator privileges on Windows / Linux.
settings.serviceContainer: This daemon runs in a container: the container runtime starts and stops it, so there is no OS service to install. Manage it with your container runtime (docker ps / docker logs / docker restart), and update it by pulling a new image and recreating the container.
settings.configHint: Export all endpoints of the current account as JSON to migrate to another machine or back up.
settings.logoutHint: After you sign out, this machine no longer runs as this account, and its endpoints and mesh disconnect. The endpoints themselves are not deleted.
settings.agentIdentityHint: This client runs as a service under the API key it was installed with, so you can't sign out or switch accounts here. To run it under a different identity, reinstall the service with a new key. To take this machine offline, uninstall the service or revoke the key in the web console.
settings.agentIdentityHintContainer: This client runs as a service under the API key it was installed with, so you can't sign out or switch accounts here. To run it under a different identity, recreate the container with a new CALABI_API_KEY. To take this machine offline, stop or remove the container, or revoke the key in the web console.
settings.dragHint: Click or drag a .json file here
settings.formatHint: The file must be in calabi-config.json format (schema_version=1)
settings.dryRunDone: Dry-run: {{total}} new endpoint(s) would be created

update.applyLostConnection: The update has started; the client is restarting.
update.applying: Updating — the client will restart shortly.
update.autoOff: This client reports new versions but does not install them by itself.
update.deferHint: After this, it installs without waiting for the window or for traffic to stop.
update.deferNeverHint: Installs as soon as a version is found, whatever the time and whatever is running.
update.holdBusy: Traffic is moving through this client; it will install once things go quiet.
update.holdSecurity: Not a security update — waiting for you.
update.holdWindow: Will install during the maintenance window.
update.holdRollout: This version is being rolled out in stages; this machine's turn has not come yet.
update.mandatoryHint: This version is no longer supported, so it will update itself regardless of the setting below.
update.modeAutoHint: Installs new versions on its own, preferably during the maintenance window and while nothing is being transferred.
update.modeNotifyHint: Installs nothing on its own — security updates included. It keeps telling you they are there.
update.modeSecurityHint: Only versions marked as security updates install on their own. Everything else waits for you.
update.reasonBadManifest: The update manifest was rejected. Nothing was installed.
update.reasonGeneric: This client cannot install updates itself — please update it manually.
update.reasonManualPlatform: This platform has no automatic update. Download and install the new version by hand.
update.reasonNotService: This daemon is not running as a privileged OS service, so it cannot replace itself. Reinstall it with `calabi daemon install --system`.
update.reasonContainer: This client runs in a container, so it updates by image: pull the new image and recreate the container.
update.tagTipApply: You can install it from Settings.
update.tagTipManual: Needs a manual update — see Settings.
update.windowLabel: Only update during a maintenance window
update.reasonManagedElsewhere: This copy was not installed by the Calabi installer (for example Homebrew, scoop, or an extracted archive), so it does not update itself. Update it the way you installed it.
update.orgMaxDefer: Your organization allows holding an update back for at most {{n}} days.
update.orgNoDefer: Your organization does not allow holding updates back.

serviceMode.agentTooltip: This client runs under a fixed identity ({{identity}}); the local console is read-only. Manage endpoints from the web console. To change the identity, reinstall the service with a different API key.
serviceMode.agentTooltipContainer: This client runs under a fixed identity ({{identity}}); the local console is read-only. Manage endpoints from the web console. To change the identity, recreate the container with a different CALABI_API_KEY.
serviceMode.agentManageTooltip: This client runs under a fixed identity ({{identity}}). You can manage this organization's endpoints here. To change the identity, reinstall the service with a different API key.
serviceMode.agentManageTooltipContainer: This client runs under a fixed identity ({{identity}}). You can manage this organization's endpoints here. To change the identity, recreate the container with a different CALABI_API_KEY.
serviceMode.tunnelsReadonly: Read-only in agent mode — manage endpoints from the web console
serviceMode.agentBannerDesc: This client runs as a service under a pinned API-key identity. Create, edit, and delete endpoints from the web console.
serviceMode.agentManageBannerDesc: This client runs as a service under a pinned API-key identity with the tunnel.write scope. You can manage this organization's endpoints here, just like the web console. Sign-in and org switching stay disabled.

login.title: Sign in to Calabi
login.subtitle: Local client console
login.totpPrompt: Two-factor authentication is on for this account — enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app below.
login.totpInvalid: That verification code didn't match. Check your authenticator app and try again.
login.registerPre: Don't have an account? Register via the

consoleLock.title: Unlock this console
consoleLock.subtitle: You're opening this client's console from another machine.
consoleLock.throttled: Too many attempts. Try again in {{seconds}} seconds.
consoleLock.failed: Couldn't unlock the console. Try again.
consoleLock.where: The daemon prints this secret in its log at startup when the console listens beyond its own machine (for a container: docker logs). It's also saved in the file console-secret in the daemon's data directory, and you can choose your own with CALABI_STATUS_SECRET.
consoleLock.unavailable: This console only accepts connections from its own machine. Open it there, or give the daemon an unlock secret (CALABI_STATUS_SECRET) to allow remote access.

tools.title: Tools / Diagnostics
tools.scanInfo: Lists this machine's listening ports and the address each is bound to
tools.scanInfoDesc: Reads this machine's own listening-socket table locally — nothing leaves the machine, and it never goes to the coordinator. Where the platform can't be enumerated it falls back to a TCP handshake against 127.0.0.1 + ::1 on the common dev ports (extend with CALABI_PROBE_PORTS=3001,4500).
tools.noPortsFound: No listening ports found — your dev server may not be running yet
tools.meshLoopbackOnlyTip: This port only listens on 127.0.0.1, so no other mesh device can reach it. Bind it to 0.0.0.0 or to this machine's overlay address.
tools.meshNotProbedTip: This machine isn't on the mesh right now, so reachability couldn't be checked.

presence.onlineHint: Connected to the coordinator. File reception must be enabled separately.
presence.offlineHint: Not currently connected to the coordinator.
presence.unknownHint: Device presence is unavailable. Please check again later.

mesh.title: Mesh
mesh.homeRelayTip: Where other devices send to reach this one when relayed. This device picks it by latency — it does not follow the region chosen at the top right. With Node set to Platform it is picked among platform relays; with Self-hosted, your own relays come first.
mesh.homeRelayTipSelfHosted: Where other devices send to reach this one when relayed. This device picks it by latency, among the server's relays.
mesh.peerRelayTip: Traffic to this peer goes through this relay. The peer picks it, so it is often not this device's own.
mesh.stopConfirm: Stop mesh on this machine? It leaves the meshnet until you start it again.
mesh.pausedDesc: Mesh is stopped on this machine.
mesh.pausedHint: This device left the meshnet. Click Start to rejoin.
mesh.blockedBanner: This machine is refusing all incoming connections
mesh.blockedBannerHelp: Peers can see it and it can still reach them, but nothing can open a connection to it. Turn it off under Network settings → Accept from the mesh.
mesh.unreachableNote: This organization has {{count}} more device(s) that the access rules do not let this machine reach. Ask an owner or admin if you need one of them.
mesh.notConfigured: Mesh is not configured on this daemon.
mesh.notConfiguredHint: Add a mesh: block (coord / relay / auth_key) to the daemon config, then restart.
mesh.unavailable: Mesh status is unavailable on this daemon.

adv.routesHelp: CIDRs on this machine's LAN to offer to the mesh, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24. Peers reach them through this device.
adv.exitNodeHelp: Other devices can route their internet traffic out through this machine.
adv.useExit: Route my traffic through an exit device
adv.useExitHelp: This machine's default traffic goes through the named exit peer (its name or overlay IP). Leave empty for none.
adv.saved: Saved — the mesh session restarts to apply it.
adv.noForward: This device is advertising these but cannot forward - subnet routing and exit devices are automated on Linux only, so traffic peers send here is dropped. Turn them off, or run the router on a Linux device.
adv.noForwardLocked: Unavailable on this device: subnet routing and exit devices need packet forwarding, which is automated on Linux only. Advertising without it would send peers' traffic to a dead end.
adv.aliasHelp: Every published subnet is automatically given a unique stand-in prefix, with the last part unchanged: .222 stays .222. Peers reach it there, so a peer whose own LAN uses the same addresses can still get through. Takes an admin approving the route.
adv.aliasPending: Waiting for the coordinator to assign addresses.
adv.aliasRefused: Some subnets could not be given an address
adv.aliasBudget: Your organisation is using {{used}} of {{total}} alias addresses. These routes still work for peers whose own network does not clash with them; the ones that clash cannot reach them. Ask an administrator to raise the limit.
adv.acceptHelp: Off by default. An accepted route enters this machine's routing table — if it covers a host that also connects to services on this machine, the replies go into the mesh and those connections stall.
adv.blockIncomingHelp: Nobody on the mesh can open a connection to this machine, whatever the access rules allow. Connections this machine starts still work, and their replies still come back.
adv.excludesHelp: Accept the rest, except these. Excluding a range also refuses the more specific prefixes inside it.
adv.routeTooBroad: Routes wider than /24 cannot be published — publish the specific /24 subnets you need, e.g. {{suggest}}.
adv.aliasUnsupported: This machine cannot install stand-in rules
adv.aliasUnsupportedHelp: They need iptables with the xt_NETMAP target. The subnets are published under their real addresses instead, so peers whose own network collides with them cannot reach them.
adv.tipLive: Other devices can reach this subnet now.
adv.tipPending: Submitted, not in effect yet: other devices can reach it once it is approved.
adv.tipUnsaved: It is submitted to the mesh when you save.
adv.tipOffline: The mesh is not connected, so other devices cannot reach it right now.
adv.tipExitApproved: Other devices can now choose this machine as their exit device.
adv.tipExitPending: Submitted, not in effect yet: other devices can choose it once it is approved.
adv.pendingTitle: {{count}} subnet(s) pending approval — other devices cannot reach them yet
adv.pendingWhere: In the web console: Approve or revoke subnets in the Subnets tab action column; review or manage exit authorization in the Devices tab action column.
adv.pendingDevice: This device itself is still waiting to be approved; nothing it offers takes effect until then.
adv.aliasAfterApproval: Assigned once the route is approved.

mesh.orgSwitching: This device is still on {{org}}'s mesh; it is re-enrolling into the organization you just switched to.

svc.introDesc: This is a declaration only — an admin confirms it in the web console before any svc: access rule matches it. A port bound to 127.0.0.1 cannot be reached from the mesh; bind it to 0.0.0.0 before declaring.
svc.declared: Declared — waiting for an admin to confirm
svc.publishedTip: Already published as the endpoint «{{name}}». Manage it on the Endpoints page.
svc.fromConfigTip: This entry comes from --mesh-service or the config file. Change it there; removing it here would be re-declared at the next restart.
svc.reachOkTip: Devices on the mesh can reach this service.
svc.reachLoopbackTip: The service only listens on 127.0.0.1, so other mesh devices can't reach it. Bind it to 0.0.0.0.
svc.reachRemoteTip: The service points at {{target}}, which isn't on this device; the mesh doesn't forward there. Move it onto this device (listen on 0.0.0.0), or enable subnet routing for this device.
svc.reachDownTip: The device can't even reach the service's local address, so the app is probably not running.
svc.reachUnknownTip: No result yet — usually within a minute. UDP services aren't probed.
svc.targetTip: What this machine dials when it checks itself, and the local address used if this service is published as an endpoint. Mesh traffic does NOT pass through it — a peer’s packet arrives on this machine’s mesh address.
svc.fromConsoleTip: A manager registered this one in the web console. This machine still self-checks it, but editing and removing it belong there — adding another one here under the same name would just leave two records, only one of them authorized.
svc.nameInvalid: Use a-z, 0-9 and - only — no spaces, and not starting or ending with -

mesh.relayRttHint: One leg: this machine to the relay. Not comparable to a direct path's end-to-end RTT.

peerDetails.unavailable: This device is no longer in the peer list

selfHosted.title: Connect to a self-hosted server
selfHosted.subtitle: Join with the invite link your server gives you.
selfHosted.meshHint: An invite link from calabi-coord invite, or the coordinator's host:port.
selfHosted.fingerprintHint: Optional. Without it, you'll be shown the coordinator's certificate to check.
selfHosted.plaintextWarn: The key crosses the network unencrypted.
selfHosted.current: Now connected to {{server}}. Fill this in to replace it.
selfHosted.switching: Connecting — the client is restarting in self-hosted mode…
selfHosted.confirmBody: This computer doesn't know the coordinator's certificate yet. Compare this fingerprint with the one the server prints:
selfHosted.signedInBody: This computer is signed in to calabi.net ({{email}}). It signs out before connecting to your server.
selfHosted.cannotJoinAgent: This client runs as a service with an API key and can't be switched from here.
selfHosted.cannotJoinForced: CALABI_MODE is set for this client. Remove it to switch here.
selfHosted.notManaged: This client runs the config file {{path}}. To change servers, edit that file.

err.bad_link: That isn't a valid invite link.
err.key_refused: The key wasn't accepted. It may be used up, expired or revoked.
err.pin_mismatch: The server's certificate doesn't match the fingerprint.
err.no_tls: The server doesn't use TLS. Choose No encryption only if you mean to.
err.disabled: This computer is disabled on that server.
err.full: That network has no room for another device.

selfHosted.leaveBody: This computer leaves your server and returns to the calabi.net sign-in page.
selfHosted.leaveTunnels: The {{n}} endpoints set up in this console are removed with it.
selfHosted.notConnectedTitle: Not connected to a server yet
selfHosted.notConnectedBody: Join this computer to your own server with an invite link.
selfHosted.certBody: {{server}} now presents a different certificate, so this computer stopped connecting to it. If you replaced it, check the new fingerprint against the server and trust it.
selfHosted.certWasTrusted: A certificate your system or CA trusted
selfHosted.certTrust: It matches — trust the new certificate
selfHosted.certChangedAgain: The server now presents yet another certificate. Check again.
selfHosted.needsInvite: The coordinator no longer accepts this computer. Join again with a new invite.
selfHosted.disabledBanner: This computer is disabled on the coordinator.
selfHosted.meshTunnelsHint: From every device running the client daemon
selfHosted.noTunnels: No device on this network has an endpoint.
selfHosted.usageUnavailable: The coordinator keeps no traffic records (it has no database).
selfHosted.meshSwitchHint: Off, this computer leaves the mesh. Its endpoints keep working.
selfHosted.awaitingApprovalBanner: Waiting for the server's administrator to approve this computer.

edgeState.no_edge: The server has no edge yet
